correctness.rationale: For each even N, conditional switch generating function exactly equals S_N(su)/S_N(u) by uniform probability of same-switch words. Pemmasani uniform Bessel bound controls it when T_N^2/N->0; Chernoff yields switch-count concentration to relative o(1/log T_N). Given switch count and first sign, positive/negative run lengths are independent uniform compositions of N/2, coupled with independent exponential spacings with collision error O(T_N^2/N). Exponential extremes converge as two independent point processes; each shifts by -log2 to intensity e^-x/2. Replacing K_N with T_N is uniformly o_p(1) for extreme points. The proof includes all needed hypotheses and no extrapolation from finite experiments; verify.py passed 285 checks.

value.rationale: The equal-occupation rare-switch Markov bridge arises naturally at Pemmasani’s endpoint–center coexistence threshold. The theorem determines the full two-color extremal domain geometry, including independent rare-event counts and the universal Gumbel longest run, across a nontrivial scaling regime, rather than only the number of switches or an arbitrary finite slice. It answers a structural question not encoded by central-bin crossing probabilities.
